thread:
Clara: Heads-up 10x Labs (customer_id: tenx-001) disputed INV-20260811. They were charged $15,600 in burst/overage on top of their 10-GPU reserved commit. They insist their traffic profile was steady. Invoice: https://invoices.redwood/INV-20260811.pdf. Can billing triage?

Ravi: Pulling the usage export and recent router logs now: s3://billing-exports/tenx-001/2026-08.csv. BILL-3379 created.

billing-bot: Export ready tenx-001/2026-08.csv (s3://billing-exports/tenx-001/2026-08.csv). Summary: total tokens 4.1B, burst tokens 260M, burst charges $15,600.

Ivy: CS says 10x uses a rate-limited ingestion buffer and would have seen large spikes if this was real. They shared app traces showing a steady 200QPS. Support #4922.

Ravi: Running a quick aggregation to look for high-cost node types and sudden region shifts:
```sql
SELECT date_trunc('minute', ts) as minute, node_type, sum(tokens) as tokens
FROM dedicated_usage
WHERE customer_id='tenx-001' AND ts BETWEEN '2026-08-01' AND '2026-08-15'
GROUP BY minute, node_type
ORDER BY minute;
```
Notable: on 2026-08-11 09:42-09:50 UTC there are many requests billed on node_type='a100-higher' in eu-central-1, despite their commit pool being in us-east-1 (10x has geo-locking on their commit). Looks like cross-region routing happened.

Clara: Cross-region routing would explain the cost delta. Do we have an automated fallback that moves traffic to the nearest pool if a region reports degraded capacity? That could bypass geo-locking.

Ravi: Found router logs showing an emergency re-route event at 09:41:58 UTC when eu-central-1 reported capacity available but the cluster metadata indicated the customer's commit in us-east-1 was temporarily marked unhealthy due to a control-plane race. Router applied fallback 'route_to_healthy' which ignored the customer's geo_lock flag. INF-7962 opened.

Ivy: 10x specifically enabled geo_lock in their Dedicated config: allow_geo_failover=false. If our router ignored that, this is on us.

Ravi: Action items: 1) Recompute usage attributing affected tokens back to their us-east-1 commit pricing and mark the eu-central rows as routing_error_nonbillable. 2) Open infra ticket to ensure geo_lock is enforced even during failovers. 3) Prepare credit proposal.

billing-bot: BILL-3379 logged: provisional investigation started. INF-7962 created: enforce geo_lock during routing fallback.

Ravi: Corrected export posted s3://billing-exports/tenx-001/corrections/2026-08-reattrib.csv. Affected tokens = 138M. Differential (eu-central on-demand vs us-east commit rate) = $12,900.

Clara: Recommend provisional credit equal to differential $12,900 plus a $1,000 goodwill SLA credit for operational impact = $13,900. Seek Finance approval and legal sign-off for any statement about "routing error" in customer comms.

Ivy: Customer is escalating procurement hold. We should move fast. Legal, please review the proposed customer note for tone: we want to acknowledge the error and commit to fixes without over-assigning liability.

legal: Reviewing. Suggest language: "We identified a routing configuration error that caused a temporary misattribution of requests to a different region, resulting in higher charges. We have corrected the billing records and applied a credit of $13,900 while we implement a permanent fix." Avoids "liability" term. Approved.

Clara: Okay Finance approval request: provisionally credit up to $14,000 to INV-20260811 (applied now) pending INF-7962 verification and final reconciliation. Approvers: @Clara (Finance), @Ravi (Billing lead).

Ravi: I approve. Applying provisional credit now and annotating invoice: "Provisional routing differential credit - under review". billing-bot: provisional credit $13,900 applied to INV-20260811 and ticket BILL-3379 updated.

billing-bot: Notification sent to tenx-001 support contact and linked support #4922.

Ivy: Sent customer message: "We've applied a provisional credit of $13,900 while we correct our routing and billing records. We'll follow up within 72 hours with final reconciliation and a description of the fix. Thank you for your patience." They replied: "Appreciate the quick action; please confirm when fixed."

Ravi: INF-7962 validated the router logic: root cause = control-plane metadata staleness during a scaling window. Patch merged to ensure geo_lock is honored even if health reports are inconsistent. PM-1071 created for regression tests.

Ravi: Final reconciliation: differential confirmed $12,900. Since provisional credit was $13,900, we applied an extra $1,000 as goodwill. Final credit to keep = $13,900. Approving final close.

Clara: Approved. Apply final credit $13,900 and close BILL-3379. Also schedule a post-mortem with infra and product to add a monitoring alert that would detect geo_lock overrides.

billing-bot: BILL-3379 closed. Final credit applied: $13,900 to INV-20260811. Artifacts: s3://billing-exports/tenx-001/corrections/2026-08-reattrib.csv. Notification sent to tenx-001 and procurement.

Ivy: Customer confirmed receipt of credit and is proceeding with contract signature. :tada:

Clara: Great work all. Please add PM-1071 and INF-7962 follow-ups to the next billing retro. Closing thread.
